# Genre lens index

Start with the shared chapter/book analysis in `SKILL.md`, then use only the relevant lenses below. Genre identification can be uncertain and works can blend genres; state a brief, qualified classification if it matters. These lenses add questions, not mandatory output headings. Use evidence from the supplied work and respect the chapter spoiler boundary.

- [Mystery and thriller](./mystery-thriller.md)
- [Fantasy and science fiction](./speculative-fiction.md)
- [Romance](./romance.md)
- [Horror](./horror.md)
- [Historical fiction](./historical-fiction.md)
- [Literary fiction](./literary-fiction.md)
- [Nonfiction and memoir](./nonfiction-memoir.md)
- [Adventure and quest narratives](./adventure-quest.md)
- [Comedy and satire](./comedy-satire.md)
- [Coming-of-age and young adult](./coming-of-age.md)
- [Family saga and social drama](./family-saga-drama.md)
- [War and political fiction](./war-political.md)

For a genre not listed, infer a small set of relevant craft questions from the work's form and stated purpose; do not invent genre conventions or force a generic checklist. Consult external sources only when needed, and distinguish source-verified context from textual interpretation.
